mainTopic: When may a woman who finds a stain on a garment she lent blame it on the borrower: a נׇכְרִית, a woman in a period of impurity, or one impure from an earlier stain?
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב's ruling: a woman who lent her garment to a נׇכְרִית may blame a stain on her only if that woman already sees blood. רב learns this by comparing the נׇכְרִית to a נדה. רב ששת calls this a mistake, citing a ברייתא where even רבי מאיר only requires that she be fit to see. רבא shows from another ברייתא that רבי מאיר is actually the lenient view, so the תנא קמא requires one who actually sees, just like רב. Next comes a ברייתא about lending a garment to a שומרת יום כנגד יום or a סופרת שבעה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets the lender blame the stain on the borrower, while רבי says both women are ruined, though both agree in cases where the borrower loses nothing. רב חסדא links this disagreement to two people on two paths, רב אדא disputes the comparison, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא rules that everyone agrees in the paths case. Finally, רבי יוחנן asks whether a stain may be blamed on a woman already impure from a stain. The answer is no, and a ברייתא that seems to contradict itself on this point gets three answers; רב אשי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רב's ruling: the נׇכְרִית must be one who sees blood
steps.stepSummary: The last word of רב's statement: the stain may be blamed on a נׇכְרִית who is 'seeing', meaning she has already had a menstrual flow.
steps.simpleTranslation: (The נׇכְרִית that the משנה means is one) who sees blood.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing רב's statement about the משנה: you may only blame the stain on a נׇכְרִית who has already had a period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says 'a נׇכְרִית'. רב narrows it down. Being old enough is not enough; she must have actually seen blood at least once.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who sees': a woman who has already had a menstrual flow
A non-Jewish woman
A blood stain found on a garment

phrases.english: who sees.
phrases.notes: This finishes רב's statement: the נׇכְרִית has to be a woman who already has her period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's statement, which began just before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stain may be blamed only on a נׇכְרִית who has already actually seen menstrual blood.

steps.title: Where does רב get this from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source in the משנה shows that the נׇכְרִית must be one who already sees blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where (do we know this)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב knows the משנה means a נׇכְרִית who already sees blood. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say 'who sees'. So the גמרא wants to know which clue in the wording led רב to add this condition.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From what?': where do we learn this?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the משנה shows that the נׇכְרִית must already be seeing blood?

steps.title: The נׇכְרִית is compared to a נדה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions the נׇכְרִית together with a נדה. A נדה is a woman who sees blood, so the נׇכְרִית must also be one who sees blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is like a נדה. Just as a נדה is a woman who sees blood, so too the נׇכְרִית is one who sees blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה treats the נׇכְרִית like a נדה. A נדה has already seen blood, so the נׇכְרִית must have too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a comparison (דומיא). The two cases sit side by side in the משנה, so they should share the same feature. That feature is a woman who actually sees blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Similar to': a comparison between two cases
A woman who is impure because of her menstrual flow
'Who sees': who actually experiences blood

phrases.english: Similar to a menstruating woman:
just as a menstruating woman is one who sees,
so too, a gentile woman who sees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה compares the נׇכְרִית to a נדה, who already sees blood, so the נׇכְרִית must also be one who sees.

steps.title: רב ששת: רב must have said this half asleep
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת sharply rejects רב's ruling and says it is a mistake, as if רב said it while dozing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: רב said this teaching while he was dozing and lying down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב's ruling and calls it a mistake. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Dozing and lying down' is a strong way of saying the ruling cannot be right. רב ששת thinks no תנא requires the נׇכְרִית to actually see blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Dozing and lying down': said without full attention, meaning a mistake
A teaching or ruling

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a story about רב actually sleeping. It is a sharp way of saying 'this ruling must be a mistake.'

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says:
when Rav was dozing and lying down
he said this teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָיֵים וְשָׁכֵיב רַב אַמְרַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from steps 1 and 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement that the נׇכְרִית already be seeing blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No תנא requires actual seeing, so רב's ruling stands against all opinions.

steps.title: The ברייתא: even רבי מאיר only requires 'fit to see'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says she may blame the stain on a נׇכְרִית. רבי מאיר says only on one fit to see blood. Even רבי מאיר, who seems strictest, does not require that she actually saw blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: She may blame it on a נׇכְרִית. רבי מאיר says: on a נׇכְרִית who is fit to see blood. Even רבי מאיר only said 'fit to see'. Actually seeing is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a ברייתא as proof against רב. Even the stricter view there only needs the נׇכְרִית to be old enough to see blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת reads the תנא קמא as allowing any נׇכְרִית at all, and רבי מאיר as adding a stricter condition. If the strictest view only demands 'fit to see', then nobody demands 'actually sees' as רב does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hangs it on': she may blame the stain on someone else
Fit to see: old enough to have a menstrual flow
It is not necessary

phrases.english: As it is taught: she attributes it to the gentile woman.
phrases.notes: This is the case of a woman who lent her garment to a נׇכְרִית and then found a stain on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
to a gentile woman who is fit to see.
And even Rabbi Meir says only
one who is fit to see,
but one who actually sees is not necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind רב ששת's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That no תנא requires the נׇכְרִית to actually see blood
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of תולה בנכרית with רבי מאיר's condition 'ראויה לראות'

steps.title: רבא: רבי מאיר is the lenient one
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב ששת's reading. רבי מאיר is lenient, not strict, so the תנא קמא is the stricter view and requires a נׇכְרִית who actually sees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do you really think רבי מאיר is being strict? רבי מאיר is being lenient!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ששת and says he read the ברייתא backwards. רבי מאיר is the lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר is lenient with 'fit to see', then the תנא קמא must be stricter. The תנא קמא allows blaming only a נׇכְרִית who has actually seen blood. So רב is simply following the תנא קמא, and רב ששת's attack falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And do you think so?': a challenge to someone's assumption
To be strict
To be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: It all depends on who is strict in the ברייתא. רב ששת thought רבי מאיר was strict. רבא says רבי מאיר is lenient ('fit to see' is enough), so the תנא קמא requires actually seeing, just like רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's ruling has a תנא behind it, the תנא קמא of the ברייתא. So it is not a mistake.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And do you understand Rabbi Meir as being stringent?
Rabbi Meir is lenient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's reading of the ברייתא in step 5, defending רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ששת's assumption that רבי מאיר is the stricter opinion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר's 'fit to see' is a leniency. The תנא קמא is stricter and requires a woman who actually sees, which supports רב.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר is the lenient one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the תנא קמא does not let her blame the stain on a נכרית, while רבי מאיר does. This supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: She may not blame the stain on a נכרית. רבי מאיר says: She may blame it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what רבא said: רבי מאיר is the lenient opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, the תנא קמא forbids blaming the stain on a נכרית, and רבי מאיר permits it. So רבי מאיר is clearly the more lenient side, just as רבא claimed. That makes the תנא קמא the stricter side.

keyTerms.meaning: She may blame (attribute) the stain on someone else
A non-Jewish woman
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: As it is taught: She may not blame it on a non-Jewish woman,
phrases.notes: This is about a woman who lent her garment and later found a blood stain on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: She may blame it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim from step 6 that רבי מאיר is lenient.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי מאיר is the lenient opinion
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which the תנא קמא says אינה תולה and רבי מאיר says תולה

steps.title: But then the first ברייתא is a problem
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא forbids blaming a נכרית, how can the earlier ברייתא have the תנא קמא allowing it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, that other ברייתא is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a clash between this ברייתא and the earlier one from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier ברייתא, the תנא קמא allowed blaming the stain on a נכרית. Here, the תנא קמא says she may not. Both cannot be read simply, so the גמרא has to explain how they fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a problem
That one (the other ברייתא)

phrases.english: But then that one is difficult!
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא from step 5, where the תנא קמא allowed blaming the stain on a נכרית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof in step 7 creates a contradiction with the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא from step 5, where the תנא קמא permits blaming the stain on a נכרית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא has the תנא קמא permitting it and the other has the תנא קמא forbidding it.

steps.title: Reading it as one who sees versus one fit to see
steps.stepSummary: Explain the first ברייתא this way: the תנא קמא allows it only for a נכרית who actually sees. רבי מאיר allows it even for one who is only fit to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: Answer it like this: The תנא קמא allows it provided that she actually sees blood. רבי מאיר says: Even if she is only fit to see blood, and even though she has not actually seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by explaining exactly what each opinion in the first ברייתא requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows blaming only a נכרית who already sees blood. That is why the second ברייתא could say he does not allow it, since it means a נכרית who does not see. רבי מאיר is more lenient: being fit to see is enough. This fits רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Answer it like this; explain it this way
A woman who actually sees menstrual blood
Fit (old enough) to see blood, even if she has not yet

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא: the תנא קמא requires a נכרית who actually sees blood, and רבי מאיר is satisfied with one who is merely fit to see.

phrases.english: Answer it like this: And provided that she sees.
phrases.notes: This is added to the תנא קמא's words: she may blame a נכרית only if that woman already sees blood.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: On one who is fit to see,
and even though she does not see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא by adding a condition to the תנא קמא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא allows blaming the stain on any נכרית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא allows it only for a נכרית who actually sees. רבי מאיר allows it even for one who is only fit to see.

steps.title: Blaming a stain on a שומרת יום כנגד יום or a סופרת שבעה
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, she may blame the stain on a שומרת יום כנגד יום on her second day, or on a סופרת שבעה who has not yet immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: She may blame the stain on a woman who keeps a day for a day, if it is on her second day, and on a woman counting seven clean days who has not yet immersed. So the lender is fixed and her friend is ruined. These are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about lending a garment to a woman who is in the middle of a period of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These borrowers are not women known to see blood right now, yet רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still lets the lender blame the stain on them. The result is that the lender stays pure, while the borrower's process toward purity is ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood in her זיבה days and must keep one clean day after it
A woman counting seven clean days
She immersed in a מקוה
Fixed; her status stays pure
Ruined; her status is spoiled

steps.confusionAlert: "Her second day" means the borrower's second day, the clean day she is keeping. It does not mean the second day of the loan.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: She may blame it
on a woman who keeps a day for a day,
on her second day.
phrases.notes: That is the day after she saw blood, when she is waiting out her clean day.

phrases.english: And on one counting seven who has not immersed,
therefore she is fixed
phrases.notes: "She" is the woman who lent the garment.

phrases.english: and her friend is ruined,
the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on blaming a stain on a Jewish borrower who is in a period of impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: she may blame the stain on a שומרת יום כנגד יום on her second day, or on a סופרת שבעה who has not immersed. The lender stays pure and the borrower is ruined.

steps.title: רבי says she may not blame it on them
steps.stepSummary: רבי disagrees: she may not blame the stain on these women, so both women are ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: She may not blame it on them. So both of them are ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי's opposing view on the same cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not let the lender shift the stain onto these borrowers. So the lender is impure because of the stain. The borrower is also ruined, since the stain might be hers. Out of doubt, both are treated strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
Therefore

phrases.english: Rabbi says: She may not blame it,
therefore both of them are ruined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: no blaming the stain on these women, so both the lender and the borrower are ruined.

steps.title: Both agree about the first day
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that she may blame the stain on a שומרת יום כנגד יום if it is that woman's first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that she may blame it on a woman who keeps a day for a day, on her first day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a case where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On her first day, the borrower already saw blood and is already impure. Blaming the stain on her does not make her status any worse. So even רבי lets the lender blame the stain on her.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree
On her first day (the day she saw blood)

steps.whatToRemember: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets the lender blame a stain on a woman in the middle of becoming pure, even though it ruins that woman's status. רבי does not. Both allow it on the first day of a שומרת יום כנגד יום, since it costs her nothing extra.

phrases.english: And they agree that she may blame it
on a woman who keeps a day for a day,
on her first day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the dispute from steps 10 and 11 with a case both sides agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees she may blame the stain on a שומרת יום כנגד יום on her first day.

steps.title: Both agree: a woman in her pure-blood days, and a virgin
steps.stepSummary: The list of agreed cases continues. Both רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי agree she may blame the stain on a woman sitting in her days of דם טוהר, or on a בתולה whose blood is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they also agree that she may blame the stain on a woman sitting in her days of pure blood, and on a virgin whose blood is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list from step 12 of cases where both sides agree the stain may be blamed on the other woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first day of a שומרת יום כנגד יום, these women lose nothing when the stain is blamed on them, because blood they see now does not make them impure. Since nobody is harmed, both תנאים allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman after childbirth during the set days when blood she sees is pure
A virgin, here right after her first relations
Her blood is pure, so it is assumed to come from the wound and not from נדה

phrases.english: And on a woman sitting in the days of pure blood,
phrases.notes: This is a woman after childbirth. In these days, blood she sees doesn't make her impure.

phrases.english: and on a virgin whose blood is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of cases both sides agree on, begun in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees a stain may be blamed on a woman in her days of pure blood, or on a virgin whose blood is pure, because neither is harmed by it.

steps.title: Why does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל need his 'therefore' line?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא adds a 'לפיכך' (therefore) clause to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, since its result seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the 'therefore' clause of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the wording of the ברייתא and asks why an extra 'therefore' line appears in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is allowed to blame the stain on the other woman, it obviously follows that only one woman is ruined. So the 'therefore' line seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore; a line that spells out the result of a ruling
Why do I need it? A question about seemingly extra words

phrases.english: The 'therefore' of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,
phrases.notes: This is the line in his statement that spells out the result: only one woman ends up ruined.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the rulings to the wording of the ברייתא quoted in steps 10-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the 'therefore' line in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view add, if its result is obvious?

steps.title: It was said to match רבי's wording
steps.stepSummary: The 'therefore' of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches nothing new. It was said only because רבי used a 'therefore' line too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is there because of רבי's 'therefore'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra line is there only to keep the two statements parallel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא wanted both views to have the same structure. רבי's 'therefore' line is needed, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל got a matching one, even though in his case it is obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of

phrases.english: Because of Rabbi's.
phrases.notes: Since רבי's statement has a 'therefore' line, the ברייתא gave רבן שמעון בן גמליאל a matching one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause was added only to match the parallel 'therefore' line in רבי's statement.

steps.title: Then why does רבי need his 'therefore' line?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: רבי's 'therefore' line, saying both women are ruined, also seems obvious, so why is it needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need the 'therefore' clause of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: Having said רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's line is there because of רבי's, the גמרא now asks why רבי's line itself is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she may not blame the stain on the other woman, it seems obvious that both are ruined. If רבי's line is also extra, the answer in step 15 falls apart, so the גמרא must find what it teaches.

phrases.english: The 'therefore' of Rabbi,
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 15: if רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's line exists because of רבי's, what does רבי's line itself teach?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does רבי's 'therefore' line (both women are ruined) teach?

steps.title: Without it, we'd think only the woman with the stain is ruined
steps.stepSummary: רבי's 'therefore' is needed. Otherwise we might think only the woman who had the garment with her when the stain was found is ruined, and the other is not. It teaches that both are ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the woman with whom the stain was found is ruined, but the other one is not. So it teaches us that both are ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי's line rules out a reasonable mistake: that only the woman holding the garment becomes impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the stain was found with one woman, we might think it belongs to her alone. רבי's 'therefore' tells us that both women are equally in doubt, so both are ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken idea the text comes to rule out
A blood stain found on a garment
She is ruined; her status of purity is spoiled
The other one
It teaches us; tells us the correct point

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'therefore' lines are explained: רבי's teaches that both women are ruined, even the one not holding the garment. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's simply matches it.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the one with whom the stain was found is ruined,
but the other one is not ruined;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16 and closes the discussion of the 'therefore' lines.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי's 'therefore' rules out the idea that only the woman holding the stained garment is ruined. Both women are ruined.

steps.title: רב חסדא: two people on two paths is the same disagreement
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a case of one impure and one pure person who walked on two paths, one pure and one impure, depends on the disagreement between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: an impure person and a pure person walked on two paths, one pure and one impure. Here we have come to the disagreement of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא takes the disagreement about the stain and applies it to a new case of two paths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the stain case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל pins the stain on the borrower, who is already in a period of impurity, so the lender stays pure, even though this ruins the borrower. In the same way, here we might pin the impure path on the person who was already impure. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל we may do that, and the pure person stays pure. According to רבי we may not, so the pure person is also in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: One person who is impure and one who is pure
Paths
We have come to the disagreement; this case depends on an earlier argument

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the argument is not just about stains. It is a general question: when there is a doubt, can we pin it on the person who is already impure, so the other person stays pure?

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
An impure person and a pure person
who walked on two paths,
one pure and one impure,
we have come to the disagreement of
Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא טָמֵא וְטָהוֹר שֶׁהָלְכוּ בִּשְׁנֵי שְׁבִילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording of the ברייתא to applying its disagreement to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case of a pure and an impure person on a pure and an impure path depends on the disagreement of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל over pinning a doubt on the one who is not harmed.

steps.title: רב אדא: the two cases are not the same
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא argues that רבי's ruling may apply only to the two women, who were alike, and not to the two-paths case, where calling the already-impure person impure changes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא objects: רבי only said this there, because both women were alike. But here, what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא attacks רב חסדא's claim from Step 18 that the two-paths case depends on the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the women's case, both women had a presumption of purity, so blaming one of them really hurts her. That is why רבי refused to blame just one. In the two-paths case, the person who was already impure stays impure anyway, so even רבי might agree we can blame him.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to, attacks a statement
Like each other, alike
What difference does it make to us?

phrases.english: Rav Adda objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi only said his ruling there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the two women, where רבי said both are ruined.

phrases.english: because the two of them are alike,
but here, what difference does it make to us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's comparison in Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the two-paths case depends on the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cases differ: both women had a presumption of purity, but the impure traveler loses nothing by being called impure, so רבי could agree in the paths case.

steps.title: רב חסדא: she also still needs immersion
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא would answer that the woman counting a day for a day is not fully pure either, since she still needs טבילה, so the cases really are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא? He would say: in the end, she too needs immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב חסדא's defense against רב אדא's attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא said the two women were both pure, unlike the impure traveler. רב חסדא answers that the woman counting a day for a day still needs טבילה, so she is not fully pure either. Even so, רבי did not blame her, so he would not blame the impure traveler either.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, after all
Immersion in a מקוה to become pure
Needs, requires

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda, how would he answer?
In the end, she needs immersion.
phrases.notes: "She" is the woman counting a day for a day from the earlier case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא, סוֹף סוֹף אִיהִי טְבִילָה בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב חסדא against רב אדא's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the claimed difference between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman counting a day for a day was fully pure, unlike the impure traveler
steps.terutzMaskana: She still needs טבילה, so she is not fully pure, and the two cases are comparable

steps.title: Everyone agrees: blame the impure path on the impure person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא rules that in the two-paths case, everyone agrees we may attribute the impure path to the impure or doubtful person and the pure path to the pure one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: an impure person and a pure person, and even a pure person and one in doubt, who walked on two paths, one impure and one pure — we attribute the impure path to the doubtful one and the pure path to the pure one, according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought about the two-paths case, saying it is not a מחלוקת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says we may blame the impure path on the impure person, and even on someone whose impurity is only in doubt. Saying "according to everyone" means even רבי agrees. This fits רב אדא's view, not רב חסדא's.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone whose impurity is in doubt
Attributes, hangs the blame on
Paths
According to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: In the two-paths case, everyone (even רבי) agrees we blame the impure path on the person who was already impure or in doubt.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
An impure person and a pure person,
and even a pure person and one in doubt,
who walked on two paths,
one impure and one pure —
one attributes the impure path to the doubtful one
and the pure path to the pure one,
according to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ruling that matches רב אדא's position against רב חסדא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the two-paths case, the impure path is attributed to the impure or doubtful person and the pure path to the pure one, and all agree.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the two-paths case is not tied to the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Can a stain be attributed to a woman already impure from a stain?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks רבי יהודה בר ליואי whether a new כתם can be attributed to a woman who is already impure from a כתם, and says he is not asking according to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked רבי יהודה בר ליואי: what is the law about attributing a stain to a stain? According to רבי, I am not asking you.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens: can we blame a stain on a woman who is already impure because of an earlier stain? רבי יוחנן also sets up which opinion his question is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the cases involved a woman who was impure for other reasons. Now the question is about a woman who is impure only because of a כתם. רבי יוחנן says his question is not according to רבי, which prepares for the next line about whose view he is asking.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a woman's garment or body
What is the law?
According to the view of
There is no question, I am not asking

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר לֵיוַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked Rabbi Yehuda bar Livai:
What is the law about attributing a stain to a stain?
phrases.notes: He means blaming a new stain on a woman who is already impure because of an earlier stain.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi,
I am not asking you.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר לֵיוַאי: מַהוּ לִתְלוֹת כֶּתֶם בְּכֶתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about attributing stains
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a new כתם may be attributed to a woman already impure from a כתם, and not according to רבי's view

steps.title: Why the question cannot be asked according to רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses a כל שכן to show that according to רבי, a woman impure from a כתם certainly cannot have a new stain blamed on her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Think about it: in the earlier case, the woman really sees blood from her own body, and you still said the lender cannot blame the stain on her. Here, where her impurity came only from something outside her body, isn't it obvious that we can't blame the stain on her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why he said he was not asking according to רבי. According to רבי the answer is obvious, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said you cannot blame a stain even on a woman counting a day for a day, who sees blood from her own body. A woman impure only because of a כתם has a weaker link to bleeding, since her stain may have come from outside. If the stronger case is not enough, the weaker case surely isn't.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; an argument from a stronger case to a weaker one
From her own body
From the outside world, from an outside source
Attributes, hangs the blame on someone else

phrases.english: Now, if there
phrases.notes: "There" is רבי's case of lending her garment to a woman counting a day for a day.

phrases.english: where she sees blood from her own body,
you said she may not attribute it to her,
here, where it comes from an outside source,
is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the remark in step 22 that the question is not being asked according to רבי.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי, a new כתם cannot be attributed to a woman impure from a כתם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A כל שכן from רבי's ruling about the woman counting a day for a day.

steps.title: The real question according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows blaming a woman counting a day for a day, would also allow blaming a woman impure from a כתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: My question is according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Maybe only there, where she sees blood from her own body, can the stain be blamed on her. Here, where it may have come from outside, maybe it can't. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now states his actual question. It is asked according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets the lender blame the stain on a woman who bleeds from her own body. The doubt is whether a woman impure only from a כתם, which may have come from outside, is strong enough to blame. The two sides are 'only real bleeding counts' or 'no difference.'

keyTerms.meaning: You should ask; the way a real question is framed
According to the view of
Or perhaps
There is no difference

phrases.english: When I raise the question to you,
it is according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל:
perhaps it is there, where she sees blood from her own body,
that she may attribute it to her,
but here, where it comes from an outside source,
she may not attribute it to her,
or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out רבי's view, it states the question according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's leniency apply to a woman impure from a כתם, or only to one who sees blood from her body?

steps.title: We do not blame the new stain on her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר ליואי answers that the new stain cannot be attributed to a woman impure from a כתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We do not attribute it. What is the reason? Because we do not attribute it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בר ליואי answers that we do not blame the stain on her. When asked why, he repeats that we do not attribute it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer means that even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would not be lenient here. Her earlier impurity came from a stain that may have come from outside. So it is not a strong enough reason to say this new stain is hers.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not attribute or blame the stain on someone else
What is the reason?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בר ליואי holds that a new כתם cannot be blamed on a woman who is impure only because of an earlier כתם.

phrases.english: He said to him: We do not attribute it.
What is the reason?
Because we do not attribute it.
phrases.notes: It sounds circular. He means her earlier stain may have come from outside, so there is nothing solid to blame the new one on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's question from step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The new stain may not be attributed to a woman impure from a כתם, even according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to allow blaming one sitting on a stain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges with a ברייתא saying that a woman who lent her garment to one 'sitting on account of a כתם' may attribute the stain to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: We do not attribute one stain to another stain. But if she lent her garment to a non-Jewish woman, or to a woman sitting on account of a stain, she may attribute it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יהודה בר ליואי. The second part of the ברייתא seems to allow blaming the stain on a woman who is impure because of a כתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with 'we do not attribute a stain to a stain,' which matches רבי יהודה בר ליואי. But it then says that if she lent her garment to a woman 'sitting on account of a כתם,' she may attribute it. That seems to contradict his answer, and the גמרא will need to explain how both parts fit.

keyTerms.meaning: A stain on account of another stain
She lent
Her garment
A non-Jewish woman
A woman keeping days of impurity because of a stain

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא seems to argue with itself: first it says we do not attribute a stain to a stain, then it allows attributing to a woman sitting on a stain. Don't panic, because the גמרא is about to address this.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
We do not attribute a stain to a woman impure from a stain.
If she lent her garment
to a non-Jewish woman
or to a woman sitting on account of a stain,
phrases.notes: He means a woman counting days of impurity because she found a stain.

phrases.english: she may attribute it to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בר ליואי's ruling that a stain cannot be attributed to a woman impure from a כתם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly allows attributing the stain to a woman sitting on account of a כתם, which seems to contradict his ruling.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא's first part says we may not blame the stain on the other woman, while its last part says we may.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult: in the first part you said we do not blame the stain on her, and in the last part you said we do blame it on her!
steps.whatsHappening: Before dealing with רבי יוחנן's challenge, the גמרא stops to show that the ברייתא he quoted seems to argue with itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has a רישא (first part) and a סיפא (last part) that seem to talk about the same kind of woman. One part says אין תולין, so the stain stays on the lender. The other part says תולין, so the stain can be blamed on the woman who borrowed the garment. Both cannot be true as they stand, so the ברייתא needs to be explained first.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
The first part of a source
The last part of a source
We blame the stain on someone else, so the woman stays טהורה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet the answer to רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 26. The גמרא is first fixing an inner problem in the ברייתא itself.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא רבי יוחנן just quoted in step 26.

phrases.english: in the first part you said we do not attribute,
in the last part you said we do attribute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא cited in step 26 and finds it contradicts itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא about lending a garment to a woman sitting because of a כתם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא rules אין תולין and the סיפא rules תולין for what seems to be the same woman, so the ברייתא contradicts itself.

steps.title: The two parts follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The first part follows רבי and the last part follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: this part follows רבי, and that part follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is solved by saying each half of the ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא of the שומרת יום כנגד יום, רבי was strict and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was lenient. This answer assumes the same split applies to a woman impure from a כתם. So the רישא (אין תולין) follows רבי, and the סיפא (תולין) follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; introduces an answer

phrases.english: This is not difficult —
this one is רבי,
phrases.notes: Meaning the first part, which says we may not blame the stain on her.

phrases.english: and that one is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split authorship: the two clauses follow two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both parts of the ברייתא follow the same view and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא follows רבי (אין תולין) and the סיפא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (תולין).

steps.title: Both parts follow רבי: first day versus second day
steps.stepSummary: Some say both parts follow רבי. One part is about the woman's first day of impurity, and the other is about her second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: both this and that follow רבי. This one is on her first day, and that one is on her second day.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer keeps the whole ברייתא following רבי and explains that the two parts are about different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day after she found her own כתם, the other woman is impure that day anyway. Blaming the new stain on her does not hurt her, so תולין. On her second day she is no longer impure and only needs טבילה. Blaming the stain on her would make her impure for an extra day, so אין תולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; both parts follow the same view
Her first day, the day she found her own stain
Her second day, after her day of impurity has passed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי's strict rule may depend on whether blaming the stain would actually cause the other woman a new loss.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
this and that are both רבי —
this is on her first day,
phrases.notes: This is the part that allows blaming the stain on her, because she is impure that day anyway.

phrases.english: that is on her second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 27 instead of the two-תנאים answer in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (אוקימתא): first day versus second day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two parts must reflect two different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי. On her first day we blame the stain on her (תולין). On her second day we do not (אין תולין).

steps.title: רב אשי: both parts follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a third answer: the whole ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: both this and that follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and it is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a third answer and says the whole ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. This line sets up his explanation, which continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two earlier answers either split the ברייתא between two תנאים or placed all of it under רבי. רב אשי takes the opposite path and places both parts under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He has not yet explained how the two parts fit together; that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not difficult; announces that an explanation of the difference is coming

phrases.english: רב אשי said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא וְהָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל —
phrases.english: this and that are both רבן שמעון בן גמליאל —
and it is not difficult,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָא וְהָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 27, different from both step 28 and step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Single authorship (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל), with the difference between the cases still to be explained
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must be split between two תנאים, or else follow רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parts follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל; how they differ is explained in the next lines.
